Checked allocation sizes
========================

Import Sizes.module's Checked theory and write:

  (array-bytes Pair uint32_t size_t length bytes)
  (doubled-capacity uint32_t 8u capacity next)

array-bytes computes length * sizeof(element) at unbounded integer precision
and stores it in bytes when the destination type represents it. The three
leading fields are compact declaration specifiers: the element type, the
length type and the destination type. length must have the length type
exactly; bytes must be an addressable modifiable object of the destination
type. The element type must be complete. A negative signed length is not
representable as a size and fails.

doubled-capacity stores initial when capacity is zero and 2 * capacity
otherwise, when that value is representable in the count type. The count type
must be unsigned; initial and capacity must have that type exactly, and next
must be an addressable modifiable object of it.

Both macros return int 1 on success. On failure they return 0 and leave the
destination unchanged. Arguments are evaluated once, in field order, including
on failure. Neither macro introduces return, break, continue or goto, and
both nest in ordinary C expressions.

Cost
----

The check is the native overflow primitive applied to the operands as
written. When the operand types make overflow impossible, as for a uint32_t
length and a small element on a 64-bit target, the compiler removes the
check: the optimized object equals an unchecked multiplication. When overflow
is reachable the check remains and costs one multiplication with its
overflow flag. The computed size is the one the allocation uses, so the
check and the arithmetic cannot drift apart.

A comparison such as count > SIZE_MAX / sizeof(element) is false for every
uint32_t count on a 64-bit target. Compilers report it as always false, it
checks nothing there, and it still requires a separate multiplication. Pass
the narrow count itself to array-bytes; a wider intermediate copy hides the
range the compiler needs to remove impossible checks.

calloc(count, size) performs the same check internally. A separate guard in
front of calloc repeats it.

Native tests cover length, signed and destination boundaries, capacity
doubling limits, failure preservation, evaluation order, type and category
refusals, native export, removal of impossible checks, retention of reachable
checks, and identical objects against handwritten C at O0 and O2.
